subject: ventures/poshmark-fee-calculator
auditor: agent session (Claude), quality round 116, see run record
professional: an experienced Poshmark reseller / resale-business bookkeeper who reconciles Poshmark payouts; they check first that the commission tier and boundary match Poshmark's current US schedule, that payout is what actually lands (including seller-paid shipping discounts, label upgrades, state fee tax), and that offer advice near the $15 line points the right way

evidence.correctness: Source: Poshmark's own support page (support.poshmark.com) returned 503 and poshmark.com/fees 404 from this container; the schedule was confirmed from 2026 third-party sources (Closo guide updated 2026-09, conductatlas copy of Poshmark's Terms: under $15 flat $2.95, $15+ 20%) and TechCrunch 2024-10-21 (the Oct 3-23 2024 5.99% experiment reversed effective Oct 24 2024); no 2025/2026 US commission change found. Probe /tmp/claude-0/qa-posh/probe.mjs against the shipped calc.mjs, recomputed by hand from that schedule: $50 -> commission 10, payout 40; $10 -> 2.95 / 7.05 / 29.5%; $5 -> 59%; $14.75 -> 2.95 = 20% (break-even 14.75); $14.99 -> 12.04 vs $15.00 -> 12.00; $1000 -> 200; offers $40->$35 payout drop 4, $12->$8 drop 4, $20->$14 drop 4.95 with commission drop 1.05, $15->$14.99 payout +0.04; target payout 20 -> price 25, 12.03 -> 14.98. All match. Input handling: '1,200' and '$20' are rejected with 'must be a number' (not silently mis-parsed), negatives and blanks rejected. Edge departures: commissionFor uses min(2.95, price), so a $2 sale shows $0 payout though Poshmark's minimum listing price is $3 (unreachable in practice); priceForTargetPayout(-1) returns $1.95, whose computed payout is $0 not -$1 (self-inconsistent below $2.95). Core arithmetic is right on every real input, so 3.
evidence.completeness: Every feature named in README, VENTURE.yaml and index.html works end to end in calc.mjs and the page script: tier and commission, effective rate, break-even note, profit after item and prep cost, loss flag, price for a target profit, offer/bundle comparison with signed payout change and threshold-crossing notes, save/forget on device, shareable fragment link (share.mjs, tests), hand-off to where-to-sell-calculator (to-where-to-sell.mjs, tests), local usage counter. Four SEO pages and llms.txt present; served copy (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs) has no placeholder or retired origin. No TODOs or stubs found.
evidence.verification: node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs share.test.mjs to-where-to-sell.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 76 pass, 0 fail. Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: tier '<' -> '<=' (calc.mjs:71) caught; crossesThreshold '>=' -> '>' (calc.mjs:220) caught; min(FLAT_FEE, price) -> FLAT_FEE (calc.mjs:72) SURVIVED; solver flat-tier bound '<' -> '<=' (calc.mjs:92) SURVIVED, a real bug (target payout $12.05 would solve to $15.00, which pays 20% and nets $12.00); 'just over the line' note window +1 -> +5 (calc.mjs:149) SURVIVED. 3 of 5 survive: the solver's tier seam and the note boundaries are not pinned. No test checks the SEO pages' prose against compareOffer, so the contradicting claim below is invisible to the suite.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (254 lines), index.html script, share.mjs, to-where-to-sell.mjs, calc.test.mjs. Pure, dependency-free, constants exported once and reused by where-to-sell-calculator (parity test there), notes generated from constants. Defects: calc.mjs:14 comment says '20% of $2.95 is $14.75' (inverted; $2.95 is 20% of $14.75); calc.mjs:22-26 header comment says crossing below $15 'can cost the seller more than the discount itself', the opposite of what compareOffer computes and documents at :190-205; calc.mjs:85 says the overlap is $12.00-$12.05 though $12.05 needs a $15.00 price, which is percent tier; solver and commissionFor disagree under $2.95. Monetary values are unrounded floats (15.07 -> commission 3.014000...02), rounded only at display. A senior JS reviewer would accept with those fixes.
evidence.claims: Backed by calc.mjs and tests: the $2.95/20%/$15 schedule, $14.75 break-even, $50->$40, $10 -> 29.5%, $5 -> 59%, $14.99 -> $12.04 vs $15 -> $12.00, $20->$14 offer drop $4.95, $40->$35 drop $4; the Oct 2024 fee experiment and reversal dates on vs-poshmarks-how-it-works-page.html match TechCrunch (5.99% seller and buyer fees, $1/$2/$3 flat, Oct 3 to Oct 23, reversed Oct 24); the Texas seller fee tax note (index.html:121) matches valueaddedresource / Texas Public Radio (from 2025-10-01; a repeal proposal was not final as of 2026-10-24). Contradicted: vs-tracking-poshmark-payouts-in-a-spreadsheet.html:35 and :60 (and its FAQ JSON-LD at :13) say dropping from just above $15 to just below 'can cost more ... than the discount itself' and is 'the one case where accepting less money can also mean losing more of it to fees' - false by the tool's own compareOffer and by hand (commission always falls when crossing down). 'Never touches seller payout' (README:47, calc.mjs:31, index.html sale help) is false when the seller offers discounted or free shipping or pays a heavier-label upgrade, which Poshmark deducts from earnings. llms.txt:5 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' is generic boilerplate. Disclaimer, not-affiliated and verify-against-payout text present on every page.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: pricing a $16 listing with a $5 cost and judging a $14 offer -> payout $11.05, profit $6.05, and the right note that Poshmark's cut absorbed $0.25 of the $2 discount. For the typical Poshmark offer, which often carries a seller-paid shipping discount (Offer to Likers), the tool has no input and tells the user shipping never touches payout, so the payout shown overstates what lands; Texas sellers' fee tax and the seller-borne USPS $50 hazmat charge (Poshmark stopped covering it from 2026-10-19, valueaddedresource) are not modelled. A bookkeeper reconciling a payout statement would hit those gaps in the first hour. Front door: links Seller Books (in development) and a sales-report analyzer, so it serves the paid bet as a lead magnet only.
evidence.domain: Against Poshmark's US seller schedule (third-party copies of the Terms and 2026 guides; Poshmark's own pages unreachable here): tier, boundary at exactly $15.00 inclusive, whole-price (not marginal) commission and no commission on buyer-paid shipping all match. Departures a practitioner would note: seller-paid shipping discounts and label upgrades deducted from earnings not modelled; Texas seller fee tax (8.25% of 80% of the fee, per Poshmark's notice as reported) mentioned but not computed; Canada's different schedule not offered (page does say US). The fee method itself is what a practitioner would sign off, so 3.

defects.what: The spreadsheet comparison page (body and FAQ JSON-LD) tells sellers that an offer dropping a sale from just above $15 to just below it 'can cost more ... than the discount itself' and is 'the one case where accepting less money can also mean losing more of it to fees'. That is false: crossing down always lowers commission (the tool's own compareOffer, index.html FAQ and the offer page say so; $16 -> $14 loses 1.75 of a 2.00 discount). A seller could turn down an offer on this advice. The same wrong claim sits in the calc.mjs header comment (:22-26).

README, calc.mjs and the sale-price help say buyer-paid shipping 'never touches seller payout', but a seller-offered shipping discount (common on Offer to Likers) or a heavier-label upgrade is deducted from earnings. The tool has no input for it, so the payout shown overstates what lands on those sales.

Three of five seeded mutants survive, including the solver's flat-tier bound '<' -> '<=' (target payout $12.05 would then solve to $15.00, which pays 20% and nets $12.00); the min(2.95, price) floor and the 'just over the line' window are also unpinned, and no test checks the SEO pages' offer claims against compareOffer.
Texas seller fee tax (noted on the page) and the seller-borne USPS hazmat charge (Poshmark stopped covering it from 2026-10-19) are not computed, so payout differs from a Texas seller's statement.

Stale or wrong comments: '20% of $2.95 is $14.75' (inverted); overlap stated as $12.00-$12.05 though $12.05 needs a $15.00 percent-tier price; solver returns $1.95 for target payout -1 while commissionFor caps the fee at the price, so the two disagree under $2.95.
llms.txt says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', generic boilerplate; the tool computes an exact published schedule.

verdict: Does not meet the bar (claims 2, verification 2; median 3); finished (completeness 3). The arithmetic is right: every recomputed output ($50 -> $40, $10 -> 29.5%, $14.99 -> $12.04 vs $15.00 -> $12.00, the $20 -> $14 offer losing $4.95 of a $6 discount, target-price solving) matches Poshmark's US schedule of $2.95 under $15 and 20% at $15+, which 2026 sources show unchanged since the October 2024 experiment was reversed (Poshmark's own support page returned 503 here). The 76 tests pass. The gaps: the spreadsheet comparison page states the opposite of the tool's own offer finding, telling sellers that crossing below $15 can cost more than the discount; 'shipping never touches payout' ignores seller-paid shipping discounts; three of five seeded bugs survive, one of them a real solver bug at $12.05. Texas fee tax and the hazmat charge are not modelled. It is a lead magnet linking the in-development Seller Books.
